newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Retail Services sees year as forecast.
newsitem.headline: Retail Services sees year as forecast.

text.p: Queensland-based grocery buying company Retail Services Ltd said it was confident profit and dividend targets forecast in its April 1996 prospectus would be met in the current year ended June 30, 1997.

"Directors are confident targets contained in the April (1996) prospectus will be met in the year to June, including the three cents final dividend," managing director John Berry told a Morgan Stockbroking breakfast meeting.
Retail Services had forecast a net profit of A$1.7 million for the current year together with the three cents final payment making a five cents total for 1996/97.
Berry said plans by retail giant Woolworths Ltd to expand its wholesale operations through its Australian Independent Wholesalers (AIW) unit were not clear at present.
But AIW's current market volume was not enough to sustain an efficient wholesaling operation.
"To run a wholesale operation, you need throughput of at least A$150 million a year. The volume they (AIW) have taken is half that needed to run an efficient operation," Berry said.
"Where are they going to get the rest?" Berry said.

Retail Services, which organises the buying of groceries on behalf of more than 450 supermarkets under banners including Four Square, Cut Price, Buy-Rite and Thrifty T, has a long-term supply contract with leading food wholesaler, Davids Ltd.
Berry said grocery independents like Retail Services had a strong future and that his company was targeting Asia as a growth area.
Retail Services also planned to expand its Nightowl franchise grocery chain interstate with the first store already opened in Sydney, Berry said.

Retail Services was also examining the introduction of computer on-line shopping "when we find the locations" as well as opportunities to establish franchise food stores at petrol stations, Berry said.
